transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 min (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (Redwood Solutions), Alex Rivera (CTO - Ember), Maya Chen (NLP Lead), Sam Ortiz (Product), Dr. Lina Patel (Clinical)

Summary: Quick scoping call for an open-model POC focusing on clinical QA and triage suggestions. Discussed success criteria, workload sizing, shortlist of open models, quality tradeoffs (clinical domain + multilingual Spanish support), benchmarks to run, timeline and next steps.

Topics: success criteria; throughput/latency sizing; dataset and eval; model shortlist and quantization; security/compliance notes; POC timeline

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to keep this pretty focused, i'll hand to priya for a quick tech framing then we'll go through success criteria and model options, sound good?
00:12 Priya: yeah thanks jordan. hi team. quick context: ember is looking to run a 2-week POC to validate open-model options for clinical question answering and triage summarization. main constraints i heard are low-latency for interactive product, high factuality in clinical domain, and need for bilingual (en/es) support, is that correct alex?
00:26 Alex: yeah that's right, low latency for clinicians in the UI, ideally p50 <200 ms for short prompts, and p95 under 800 ms. also accuracy on our clinical testset has to be at least 92% precision for triage recommendations, otherwise ops won't sign off.
00:42 Sam: timelinewise we want to move fast—if POC looks good, we want a pilot embedded in product early Q1. so two week POC then a 6-8 week pilot.
00:51 Priya: great. quick questions on workload sizing — what qps and token volumes do you expect?
00:56 Maya: average interactive sessions are small, about 18 tokens input, 80 tokens output on average. Peak concurrent users during clinic hours ~40, so peak qps around 40-50, average qps about 7-10. monthly token budget for the product would be roughly 3M-5M tokens.
01:16 Priya: ok that's helpful. for benchmarks we'll run three profiles: interactive low-latency (single request), batch triage process (50 concurrent requests), and long-note summarization (sequences up to 4096 tokens). we'll capture p50/p95 latency, throughput, and accuracy using your evaluation prompts.
01:35 Jordan: needed success criteria recap: 1) p50 latency <200ms on our dedicated instance for short prompts; 2) triage precision >=92% on the clinical rubric; 3) cost per 1k tokens below your internal threshold (you mentioned cost sensitivity), 4) Spanish answers within 5% of English accuracy on benchmark.
01:52 Alex: yes those align. also we need audit logs and ability to disable caching for PHI-sensitive flows, we can't persist patient identifiers.
02:02 Priya: noted—Redwood supports disabling prefix cache and KV cache per-route, and we can run POC in private VPC mode if needed; for the initial POC hosted dedicated nodes are fine if you prefer.
02:13 Maya: question — for open models, how do we choose between larger models like Llama-2-13B and Mistral-Instruct variants? cost vs quality tradeoff is a big concern.
02:23 Priya: good question. for clinical domain, sometimes smaller fine-tuned instruct models actually outperform base LLMs on precision, but larger models tend to give better contextual reasoning. our plan is to test a shortlist: Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized), Mistral-Instruct-v0.2 (7B/greater), and Mistral-7B-quant (7B quantized). we may add Llama-2-70B-lite if we see gaps in reasoning, but that's heavier.
02:47 Ethan: also we'll include a lightweight retrieval-augmented config — index your de-identified clinical KB and pass top-5 docs to the model. That often improves factuality more cost-effectively than just upsizing models.
02:58 Dr. Patel: retrieval is interesting but for PHI we need the retrieval layer to live in our VPC and for Redwood to respect do-not-store flags. is that supported?
03:07 Priya: yes, we can configure retrieval connectors to your VPC or run an on-prem agent; and we can set per-route retention to zero and disable logging for those routes. we'll document this for legal.
03:19 Sam: benchmarks — can you test quantized 4-bit runs? we want to see if 4-bit quant gives sub-200ms p50 and acceptable quality.
03:27 Priya: absolutely. plan is to benchmark: base fp16 for accuracy baseline, 8-bit quant, and 4-bit quantized models with Redwood's optimized runtime kernels. we'll surface delta in accuracy on your eval set and delta in latency/cost.
03:40 Alex: what about multilingual support—our Spanish corpus includes regional colloquialisms, medical shorthand. will the models handle that?
03:48 Priya: we'll include a Spanish-focused eval set. Mistral variants usually handle Spanish decently; Llama-2-13B chat is okay but sometimes needs instruction tuning. If Spanish accuracy is off, we can try instructional fine-tuning on a small in-domain corpus or use a bilingual adaptation step during the POC.
04:05 Jordan: on timelines — proposed schedule: Jordan sends cost/plan + benchmark matrix by Th 12/03; Maya uploads de-identified prompts + rubric by 12/04; Priya provisions infra and kicks off benchmarks week of 12/07; mid-POC check-in 12/17 to review initial results; final report and recommendation 12/22. does that align with your timelines sam?
04:27 Sam: yes that's fine, just please include expected costs for both hosted-dedicated and private VPC runs in the spreadsheet.
04:33 Alex: security - we need SOC2 type II evidence and KMS integration for prod. for POC we just need the security brief and DPA.
04:41 Jordan: we'll include SOC2 attestation link and our KMS/HSM approach in the security packet; Priya will attach tech notes on encryption-in-transit and at-rest for the POC artifacts.
04:50 Maya: one more — metrics: we'll want BLEU/ROUGE for summarization, and a custom clinical precision metric for triage. are you able to run those automatically and produce a dashboard?
04:59 Priya: yes we can output evaluation metrics into the Redwood Console; we'll provide per-route dashboards with token breakdowns, p50/p95 latency, and custom eval metrics you provide.
05:10 Alex: ok can you remind me which models you'll test exactly?
05:12 Priya: shortlist: 1) Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized; fp16 baseline + 8-bit + 4-bit), 2) Mistral-Instruct-v0.2 (7B family; fp16 + 8/4-bit), 3) Mistral-7B-quant (fast low-cost option), and 4) Dolly-* style or other smaller instruct models as a low-cost baseline — we'll include a tuned 3-5B we have on file if you want. We'll capture quality vs cost tradeoffs.
05:34 Maya: please also include a baseline using your Redwood-verified open model profile numbers so we can compare to your public benchmarks.
05:40 Ethan: noted — we'll include Redwood's verified perf profiles and show kernel-level delta.
05:44 Jordan: any objections to running the initial POC on our hosted dedicated pool? it gives predictable throughput and lower setup friction. If you prefer private VPC for data residency we can pivot but that adds 1-2 days setup.
05:58 Alex: hosted dedicated is fine for initial POC, as long as the do-not-store flags are observed.
06:03 Dr. Patel: one red flag — if a model hallucinates a triage that could harm patient care, we need guardrails. can Redwood support model-level rejection thresholds and confidence scoring?
06:15 Priya: yes, we can add a rejection policy (score threshold) and confidence post-processing; we can also route low-confidence cases to human-in-the-loop flows. we'll prototype that in the POC.
closing:
06:20 Jordan: recap — action items and dates as discussed; i'll send the plan and pricing today/tomorrow, priya will start infra once we have the eval sets. thanks everyone, talk soon.
06:30 Alex: thanks all.

End of meeting.
